The attraction effect (decoy effect) is a context effect: adding a third, asymmetrically dominated option makes the target option more attractive relative to a competitor. Key terms include asymmetric dominance, decoy, target and competitor options, context-dependent preferences, preference reversal, violation of independence of irrelevant alternatives, and choice set framing.

Key terms include asymmetric dominance, context-dependent preference, preference reversal, choice architecture, and ranking/ordinal utility.
